title: Local Gateway
blurb: Certificate trunks, registration trunks, CUBE parameters, and the certificate name the cloud expects.

lessons.title: What the local gateway is
lessons.summary: The local gateway is your edge for PSTN and for PBXs such as Unified CM. Control Hub turns it into a trunk and hands you parameters to put on the device.

paragraphs: The workflow guide calls the local gateway an enterprise or partner-managed edge for PSTN and for legacy PBX interworking, including Unified CM.
Phones do not register to Webex Calling through the gateway in the multi-tenant sense. The gateway registers or presents a trunk.
Only certificate-based trunks, and only SBCs listed as compatible local gateways in Control Hub.
A random SBC on UDP 5060 is not a supported local gateway.

fault.title: UDP 5060 to the cloud
fault.symptom: A gateway sends plain UDP SIP and never establishes TLS.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: destination udp/5060, no TLS, trunk down.
fault.cause: Webex Calling signaling in the port reference is SIP TLS on 5062 or 8934.
fault.fix: Configure TLS to the documented port for the trunk type you created.

lessons.title: Certificate trunks and TCP 5062
lessons.summary: A certificate trunk signals to TCP 5062. The certificate CN or SAN has to match the FQDN or SRV name the trunk article tables out.
objectives: Separate listen port from destination port

diagram.caption: 5062 is the cloud destination for certificate trunks. The name in the certificate must match the trunk identity.

steps.detail: The trunk article tables DNS and the certificate name for each.

steps.label: Present the name
steps.detail: CN or SAN contains the identity the table requires.

paragraphs: For an FQDN trunk, the DNS A record and the certificate name are that FQDN. For an SRV trunk, the SRV name is what the certificate must carry, and the SRV target is a single A record in the article's example.
Contact headers in the table include transport=tls. UDP contact headers will not match the example.

fault.title: 403 after a hostname change
fault.symptom: The trunk FQDN was updated in Control Hub and the old certificate stayed on the router.
fault.cause: The table requires the names to match.
fault.fix: Issue a certificate with the new name, install it, and retry one call. Do not disable TLS verification.

lessons.title: Registration trunks and TCP 8934
lessons.summary: Registration-based trunks signal to TCP 8934. They are a different object from certificate trunks. Third-party SBCs do not get this shortcut.

diagram.caption: 8934 is registration. It is not a second port you add to a certificate trunk for luck.

steps.label: Choose registration
steps.detail: Use the parameters Control Hub gives you for that model.

steps.label: TCP 8934
steps.detail: The port reference's registration destination.

steps.label: Up
steps.detail: The trunk shows registered. Then place a call.

steps.label: Stop if unlisted
steps.detail: Third-party local gateways are certificate-based and must be a listed type.

paragraphs: Pick registration or certificate when you create the trunk. The ports are not a menu of both.
A firewall that opens only 5062 will pass a certificate trunk and black-hole a registration trunk.
A registered trunk can still fail media if UDP ranges are blocked. Signaling and media are separate rows in the port reference.
Test one call in each direction after the trunk shows up.

choices: Does not save a registration trunk
Use certificate trunks and must be listed

fault.title: Bench versus branch
fault.symptom: Registration works in the lab and dies at the branch firewall.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: deny tcp/8934, allow tcp/5062, trunk type=registration.
fault.cause: The branch copied the certificate-trunk rule.
fault.fix: Allow 8934 for this trunk, or rebuild it as a certificate trunk and allow 5062. Do not leave both half-configured.

sections.h: The course is the lab manual for the CLI
paragraphs: CLWXCALL's outline includes routers that support the local gateway, deployment scenarios, Control Hub settings, router settings, and troubleshooting.
This lab will not paste a full IOS configuration. The parameters are tenant-specific and the course plus the help article are the procedure.
Trunk credentials and certificate private keys do not belong in tickets or screenshots.
The public parameters, the FQDN, and the port do.

fault.title: Worked from a copied config
fault.symptom: A second site's CUBE was cloned and presents the first site's certificate name.
fault.cause: The identity table failed because the config was cloned.
fault.fix: Generate site B's parameters from its own trunk and install a matching certificate.

lessons.title: Media after the trunk is up
lessons.summary: Signaling can succeed while audio fails. ICE may remove the cloud relay. The UDP ranges in the port reference are then the whole path.

diagram.caption: SRTP media is a different row from SIP TLS.

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.detail: The dialog exists. Users still hear nothing.
steps.inspect: Do not restart the trunk first

steps.label: Did it succeed?
steps.detail: The port reference says successful ICE inside the org removes the cloud media relay.
Audio 8500-8599 and video 8600-8699 in the example.
The device optimized range in the same example.

paragraphs: The port reference lists SRTP, SRTCP, and related UDP toward Webex Calling, including ports 5004 and 9000 and the broader ranges.
RFC 3711 is the SRTP specification. You do not need to reimplement it. You need to let it through.
The article's warning is specific: when media goes direct, firewalls inside the premises have to allow those source and destination ranges.
A perimeter rule that only allows the cloud subnets will not save a direct media path.

fault.title: Silent after a 'secure' firewall change
fault.symptom: Calls connect. Audio works at home and fails in the office.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: ICE success, office firewall denies udp/8500-8699.
fault.cause: Direct media hits the inside firewall.
fault.fix: Allow the documented ranges both ways inside the site, then retest from the office network.

lessons.summary: Once the trunk is up, changes are certificate expiry, firewall drift, and dial-plan edits. The gateway is not where you add Webex Calling users.

steps.detail: On-prem patterns live there, not only on the CUBE.

steps.label: Control Hub
steps.detail: A new Webex user is a license and a number, not a dial-peer.

paragraphs: Webex Calling destinations are known to the cloud. The gateway sees what the cloud sends it and what the PBX sends it.
Adding a user only on the CUBE does not create a Webex Calling user.
Unified CM still normalizes to +E.164 in the integration guide. That work is on the cluster, on purpose.
When you migrate users off the cluster, you delete those route patterns as part of migration, not as part of gateway hygiene.

fault.title: User added on the router
fault.symptom: A new hire was given a dial-peer and no Control Hub user. The Webex App has no phone service.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: CUBE dial-peer 2108, Control Hub user absent.
fault.cause: The cloud does not learn users from the gateway.
fault.fix: Create the user, assign the license and number, and remove the mistaken dial-peer if it hijacks a range.

lessons.title: Gateway review
lessons.summary: A gateway is ready when the trunk type, the name, the ports, the one-location rule, and a call in each direction all have evidence.
objectives: Hand media and emergency to the next owners

diagram.caption: Evidence, not a screenshot of a prompt.

steps.label: Which port?
steps.detail: Say 5062 or 8934 out loud.

steps.label: Show the cert
steps.detail: CN or SAN versus the trunk FQDN or SRV. Redact the key.

steps.label: Count trunks
steps.detail: One selected.

steps.label: Two results
steps.detail: Inbound and outbound, plus an on-prem extension if that is the job.

paragraphs: Missing evidence is a fail. A story about a call last month is not evidence.
Emergency calling and contact center premise agents are explicit follow-ups, not implied by a registered trunk.

cite.label: Enhanced emergency calling for Webex Calling

paragraphs: You do not need a full IOS dump in the review packet.
You do need the trunk name, type, ports, certificate identity, location binding, and call results.

fault.title: Green trunk, failed cutover
fault.symptom: Monday morning inbound fails. The trunk still says registered. The certificate expired Sunday.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: registered=true, cert notAfter=Sunday, Monday INVITE fails.
fault.cause: Registration state was stale relative to the certificate.
fault.fix: Replace the certificate, confirm the name still matches, and place a new call. Add expiry to the monthly card.
